concepts.heading: Your Relationship Philosophy
concepts.plain: After all you have learned, it is time to decide what you believe about relationships.

concepts.heading: What Is a Relationship Philosophy?
concepts.plain: It is a guide for your choices, not a list of rules.

concepts.heading: Key Questions for Your Philosophy
concepts.plain: Ask what you value most: honesty, freedom, safety, growth, fun?

concepts.heading: A Living Document
concepts.plain: It will change over time, and that is fine.

concepts.heading: Shaped by History
concepts.plain: Your early life shaped your views. Check whether they still fit you.

options: Not a list of rules or a rigid manifesto
checks.explanation: Not a list of rules or a rigid manifesto. A relationship philosophy is not a list of rules or a rigid manifesto.

checks.prompt: Will your relationship philosophy stay the same forever?
options: Yes, once written it is fixed
checks.explanation: No, it will change. Your relationship philosophy will change. It is a living document.

3fb85402-a554-4c70-a03c-d57008224d5b.takeaway: Write down what you value in relationships and let it change as you grow.

concepts.heading: Continuing Education & SHA Resources
concepts.plain: This course is a starting point, not the finish.

concepts.heading: Recommended Books
concepts.plain: A few well-respected books are a good next step.

concepts.heading: Podcasts and Online Communities
concepts.plain: Podcasts and online groups keep you learning in an easy way.

concepts.heading: The Importance of Diverse Perspectives
concepts.plain: Learn from people whose lives are different from yours.

concepts.heading: Workshops and Conferences
concepts.plain: Workshops let you practise, which books cannot do.

concepts.heading: Evaluating Quality
concepts.plain: Not all sex ed is good. Check who is teaching it.

concepts.heading: Education vs Therapy
concepts.plain: Education gives you knowledge. Therapy gives you personal healing. They are different.

options: A foundation, not a finish line
checks.explanation: A foundation, not a finish line. This curriculum is a foundation — not a finish line.

checks.prompt: What is the difference between education and therapy?
options: Education gives knowledge and skills; therapy gives personalized healing
checks.explanation: Education gives knowledge and skills; therapy gives personalized healing. An important distinction: education provides knowledge and skills; therapy provides personalized healing and growth.

2ba78fc0-3133-405a-b3dc-98854a5cf09d.takeaway: Keep learning from good books, podcasts and workshops, and know when you need a therapist instead.

concepts.heading: Finding Professional Support
concepts.plain: Getting professional help is a way of looking after yourself and your relationships.

concepts.heading: Types of Providers
concepts.plain: Different professionals have different training. Sex therapists have extra training in sexuality.

concepts.heading: Finding the Right Provider
concepts.plain: Online directories let you search for certified people near you.

concepts.heading: What to Look For
concepts.plain: Look for someone who understands open relationships and kink and will not judge.

concepts.heading: Advocating for Yourself
concepts.plain: You are allowed to ask a provider questions before you commit.

concepts.heading: Cost and Access
concepts.plain: Help can cost a lot. Ask about lower-cost options.

concepts.heading: Normalizing Help-Seeking
concepts.plain: Going to therapy does not mean something is wrong with you.

checks.prompt: What sets AASECT-certified sex therapists apart?
checks.explanation: Specialized training in human sexuality. AASECT-certified sex therapists have completed specialized training in human sexuality beyond their general therapy license.

options: Not a sign that something is wrong with you
checks.explanation: Not a sign that something is wrong with you. Therapy is not a sign that something is wrong with you. It's an investment in your wellbeing and your relationships.

47da48b3-d4e2-4681-b989-e6b373432fcc.takeaway: Getting professional help is self-care. Look for someone who respects your relationship style.

concepts.heading: Your Growth Edge
concepts.plain: Your growth edge is the spot where your skills meet your next challenge.

concepts.heading: Identifying Your Growth Edge
concepts.plain: Notice which topics in this course felt most alive for you. Start there.

concepts.heading: Setting Intentions, Not Resolutions
concepts.plain: An intention is a direction to move in, not a pass-or-fail goal.

concepts.heading: Building Your Support Network
concepts.plain: Nobody grows alone. Build a circle of people who support you.

concepts.heading: Self-Compassion Throughout Growth
concepts.plain: Progress goes up and down. Be kind to yourself.

concepts.heading: A Closing Affirmation
concepts.plain: You have put real time into understanding yourself. That counts.

options: A direction you want to move in
checks.explanation: A direction you want to move in. An intention is a direction you want to move in. A resolution is a rigid goal with pass/fail outcomes.
Not linear. Progress is not linear. You will have setbacks, moments of confusion, and times when old patterns reassert themselves.

ba522c3f-975e-4e68-afea-5e84176b3d1a.takeaway: Pick the one area you most want to grow in, set a direction, find support and be kind to yourself.
